The requirement was taken from v4.0.3 close to as it was and the second part of the requirement (_using a well‑known and secure HTML sanitization library or framework feature._) is non-actionable "noise" that does not add anything useful to the requirement. This part should be removed.

The main point for the requirement:
If from untrusted input HTML content is accepted and that is used to be rendered later, it must be sanitized to contain only allow-listed HTML tags and attributes when using the content.

How someone implements it, what libraries they are using, is not our/ASVS business to say. We only say the security principle that must be followed.

For this requirement, I would not touch the client-side or server-side topic, the principle to achieve is the same. Also note that HTML content is often used in emails, html 2 pdf libraries etc.

If there is a special need to say something about browser-side sanitization, it should be a special case and belong to the "V3 Web Frontend Security" chapter. Also, at the moment, it (potential new requirement) could be a breaking change. I don't see the material for it at the moment.

Reviewing full thread. I think the proposal to go was already set in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/3231#issuecomment-3288137361 which took my comment into account:

So the proposal is:
> Verify that all untrusted HTML input from WYSIWYG editors or similar sources is sanitized to contain only an allow-listed set of tags and attributes before rendering.

I would also say it is a non-breaking change.

To cover all the points, it may become something like:
> Verify that all untrusted HTML input from WYSIWYG editors or similar sources is sanitized before storing or before rendering to contain only an allow-listed set of tags, attributes, and attribute values. Allow-list configuration must take into account what is safe for the application, and for each use (for example, it may require different rules for client-side and server-side rendering to be safe). Additionally, it may need to validate attribute values (for example, a src attribute value uses a safe path or URL).
